en: The Philippine Eagle uses its sharp, strong talons to catch flying lemurs and other prey in the forests of Mindanao.
The giant Rafflesia flower in Mount Kitanglad produces a foul odor resembling rotting meat to attract pollinating flies.
Filipino pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo invented an improvised bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of fish and 300 coral species.
The endangered Mindoro tamaraw, a small buffalo species, has distinct V-shaped horns and lives only in the grasslands of Mindoro.
The rare orchid Vanda sanderiana, known as the Queen of Philippine Orchids, grows high on tree branches in Mindanao forests.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which breeds in clean stagnant water, transmits the dengue virus to humans through its bite.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes and can rotate its head 180 degrees to spot insects in the dark.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a cave ecosystem where guano from bats and swiftlets supports diverse insects.
A coconut palm tree takes about 5 to 10 years to produce its first fruit after being planted from a seed.
The whale sharks visiting Donsol, Sorsogon, are filter feeders that use their wide mouths to consume tiny plankton in the ocean.
The BCG vaccine, given to Filipino babies at birth, protects infants from severe forms of the tuberculosis bacterial infection.
